evidence_reviewed: ES query covering the injection window
Health witness log: BOTH validation-enrichment AND aml-compliance independently went DOWN then RECOVERED
validation-enrichment own logs: real MongoDB driver exceptions ("Exception in monitor thread while connecting to server localhost:27017"), then HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED at 11:09:57.5

aml-compliance own logs: the SAME MongoDB connection failure signature ("connecting to server localhost:27017"), its own separate monitor thread, then HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED at 11:09:59.0 -- a service not previously known to depend on MongoDB in the code-level dependency map
Funnel: 39 PAYMENT_SUBMITTED but zero PAYMENT_VALIDATED and zero AML_SCREENING_COMPLETE anywhere in the window -- total pipeline stall past gateway

Decisive tell: two otherwise-unrelated services (validation-enrichment, aml-compliance) both fail while referencing the exact same external endpoint (localhost:27017) at nearly the same time -- the signature of a shared infrastructure dependency failing, not either services own bug
reasoning_trace: First live test of MONGODB_OUTAGE. Witness independently flagged BOTH validation-enrichment and aml-compliance DOWN, which initially looked like it might be a genuine multi-service confound (only one of two DOWN services could be the true root). But both services own log streams show the identical, specific MongoDB driver connection-failure message referencing the same localhost:27017 endpoint, each from their own independent monitor thread -- this is the actual decisive evidence, not the health-check failures themselves. Two services failing for the same stated external-dependency reason at the same time points directly at that shared dependency, not at either service individually. Conclusion reached from evidence alone, before reading the injectors own log: mongodb.
confirmation_basis: Blind conclusion (mongodb) matches the injectors own ground-truth log exactly. Real finding, not previously known: aml-compliance also has a direct MongoDB dependency (own connection/monitor thread), not just validation-enrichment as the original code-grep-based dependency map assumed -- worth correcting that mapping. Separately, the injectors own recovered flag for this incident reads False in output/live_incidents.csv (30s recovery-poll deadline was too short for MongoDB in this run; docker ps -a independently confirmed genuine recovery shortly after) -- infra-level timing note, not a fault to the blind conclusion, which is unaffected by post-recovery timing.
